title: Driving to Las Vegas and meeting Red Norvo
summary: With no rehearsal, Monk met Red and a first guitarist who soon left, replaced by Lloyd Ellis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I guess you could say pried, yeah, he pried me. And I said, 'OK. When does the gig start?' I think the job started on a Thursday, something like that, and we had a day or so to get there. And I said that I had my car here with me. I had just picked up my instrument, my clarinet, and that's what the trip took me up there. I had just picked it up and had set it up in that little room, where I was working and playing.

'Well, I got my car. I'll just drive down and meet you in Las Vegas.' He said, 'OK, and we're staying at the Tropicana Motel, across the street, there are rooms there for us. And all you have to do is... I'll see you there. I'll be there on Tuesday,' or Wednesday or whatever it was. And I said, 'Well, what about our rehearsals?' And he said, 'I don't think we need no rehearsals; this is a jazz gig and we can do it without...'

He had a kid playing guitar, and I can't think of his name because he only lasted about two or three days, that weekend, whatever, because he was so far out on pills and things... And then Red brought in Lloyd Ellis, he was a guitar player. After just a few days, Lloyd Ellis came in.

And when I met him in Las Vegas, it was almost like meeting a total stranger, meeting Red in terms of here we are and looking over the gig. I always respected him; I had so much respect for Red as a musician. That's the only way I knew of him, his music. And I was happy to be associated with him, and
he gave me the same feeling.
